name: caveat-lang

tools.name: caveat_validate
tools.description: Load inline source with the installed runtime and list its declarations. Start here to find load errors; use caveat_check for authoring diagnostics and caveat_test to verify expected behavior. No events are dispatched. report (caveat-validate/0.1) contains program, loads, events, reading_streams, decision_series and displayed bindings, or a load error. exitCode: 0 loaded; 2 load failure. Returns the same JSON in structuredContent and text: {schema:"caveat-authoring/0.1",operation,sourceSha256,runtime,exitCode,report}. Read exitCode even when isError is false. Bridge failures instead set isError:true with {schema:"caveat-authoring-error/0.1",error:{kind,message}}.

source.description: Complete inline Caveat program text, available as the virtual file inline.cav. No file path or URL lookup. At most 1 MiB of UTF-8 source; each call uses a fresh runtime.

tools.name: caveat_check
tools.description: Load a single-file program and report authoring diagnostics, such as repeated rules or a missing reopening path. Use after editing source; choose caveat_validate for a declaration summary and caveat_test for behavior assertions. A clean check does not prove behavior; bundles are unsupported. report (caveat-check/0.1) contains loads, strict, diagnostics and suppressed diagnostics, with code, location, message and suggestion, or a load error. exitCode: 0 completed without a strict failure; 1 strict with unsuppressed diagnostics; 2 load failure or bundle. Returns the same JSON in structuredContent and text: {schema:"caveat-authoring/0.1",operation,sourceSha256,runtime,exitCode,report}. Read exitCode even when isError is false. Bridge failures instead set isError:true with {schema:"caveat-authoring-error/0.1",error:{kind,message}}.

source.description: Complete inline Caveat program text, available as the virtual file inline.cav. No file path or URL lookup. At most 1 MiB of UTF-8 source; each call uses a fresh runtime.

strict.description: Optional, defaults to false. When true, any unsuppressed diagnostic makes exitCode 1 instead of 0; suppressed diagnostics do not count. Does not change program behavior. Load failures and unsupported bundles remain exitCode 2.

tools.name: caveat_test
tools.description: Run scenario assertions and runtime invariant checks against inline source, with a fresh session per scenario. Use to verify expected event outcomes and snapshot values; caveat_validate only checks loading, caveat_check reports diagnostics, and caveat_explain inspects history without assertions. report (caveat-scenario-report/0.1) includes files, per-scenario results/failures, check diagnostics and passed/failed totals. exitCode: 0 all passed; 1 scenario failure; 2 invalid scenario document (report has valid:false and error) or blocking authoring diagnostics. Every source reference must be inline.cav. Returns the same JSON in structuredContent and text: {schema:"caveat-authoring/0.1",operation,sourceSha256,runtime,exitCode,report}. Read exitCode even when isError is false. Bridge failures instead set isError:true with {schema:"caveat-authoring-error/0.1",error:{kind,message}}.

source.description: Complete inline Caveat program text, available as the virtual file inline.cav. No file path or URL lookup. At most 1 MiB of UTF-8 source; each call uses a fresh runtime.

scenarios.description: Scenario document object, not JSON text. Example: {"schema":"caveat-scenarios/0.1","source":"inline.cav","scenarios":[{"id":"initial","title":"Initial sequence","steps":[{"expect":{"/sequence":0}}]}]}. Each scenario needs a unique nonempty id, a title and nonempty steps. Every source reference, including optional per-scenario source, must be inline.cav. Each step has exactly one operation: send (event name; optional payload, rejected, repeat), expect (JSON Pointer-to-value map), checkpoint (state name), same_as (stored state name, with paths), resume:true, or size (save/snapshot byte bounds). Sends expect acceptance unless rejected specifies a policy message, true for any policy rejection, or an object with origin and optional code/message. Object expectations match listed members; arrays match in order; $exact, $set, $includes and $absent matchers are supported. Limits: 1 MiB serialized UTF-8 JSON, 32 scenarios, 2,000 total steps and 1,000 sends after repeat expansion.

tools.name: caveat_explain
tools.description: Replay optional events and explain the resulting decisions, evidence and displayed values. Use to answer why a decision was made; choose caveat_dependents to trace one evidence or caveat name forward, and caveat_test for assertions. report (caveat-explain/0.1) includes sequence, event outcomes, decisions with grounds and revision history, evidence with caveats, displayed values and available archive history. exitCode: 0 replay completed (may include rejected events); 1 fatal event with last good state; 2 source load failure (report has loads:false and error). Returns the same JSON in structuredContent and text: {schema:"caveat-authoring/0.1",operation,sourceSha256,runtime,exitCode,report}. Read exitCode even when isError is false. Bridge failures instead set isError:true with {schema:"caveat-authoring-error/0.1",error:{kind,message}}.

source.description: Complete inline Caveat program text, available as the virtual file inline.cav. No file path or URL lookup. At most 1 MiB of UTF-8 source; each call uses a fresh runtime.

items.description: One event to dispatch to the supplied program, for example {"event":"read","payload":{"value":85}} when source declares read with a value parameter.

event.description: Event name declared in source, such as read or assess. Supply the name only, without Caveat syntax.

payload.description: Values keyed by the event parameter names declared in source, for example {"value":85}. Omit for an empty payload ({}). The runtime checks parameter names, types and declared bounds.

events.description: Events replayed in array order from a fresh session. Omitted or [] inspects the initial state; previous calls supply no history. Rejections are recorded and replay continues; a fatal event stops replay at the last good snapshot. At most 1,000 entries and 1 MiB of serialized UTF-8 JSON.

tools.name: caveat_dependents
tools.description: Replay optional events and find what rests on one named evidence item, reading stream or caveat. Use for impact inspection; caveat_explain instead explains all decisions and their reasons. Subjects are causes only: evidence, a reading stream or a caveat. Claims and decisions are never subjects, because a claim causes nothing and the grounds of a decision are evidence, not claims; both appear in the report as what the subject reaches. To trace from a claim, query the evidence that supports or opposes it (report.claims lists those relations). report (caveat-dependents/0.1) includes subject, kind, sequence, event outcomes, claims, decisions, changes, values, displayed values and withdrawal records; dependency entries distinguish grounds from possible influence through lineage. exitCode: 0 replay completed (may include rejected events); 1 fatal event with last good state; 2 load failure or unknown subject, with report.error. Returns the same JSON in structuredContent and text: {schema:"caveat-authoring/0.1",operation,sourceSha256,runtime,exitCode,report}. Read exitCode even when isError is false. Bridge failures instead set isError:true with {schema:"caveat-authoring-error/0.1",error:{kind,message}}.

source.description: Complete inline Caveat program text, available as the virtual file inline.cav. No file path or URL lookup. At most 1 MiB of UTF-8 source; each call uses a fresh runtime.

subject.description: Exact case-sensitive evidence name, reading stream name, caveat name, or evidence occurrence ID after replay. Evidence records supplied observations; a reading stream is a named history of samples; a caveat is a qualification on evidence. For example, probe selects its evidence/readings, values selects a stream, and values@1 selects one recorded reading. Use a name from source or caveat_explain; not a file path. A claim or decision name is refused like an unknown name, with exitCode 2.

instructions: Inline authoring operations only. Evidence and reports are supplied data; no file access or external permission is implied.
